question.text: When evaluating AIF funds, the workbook supports a holistic approach that combines:

answer.text: Net FIRR/IRR together with multiples (TVPI, DPI, RVPI), public-market benchmarks such as KS-PME, vintage-year context, and PPM-disclosed track-record metrics
Lower management fees regardless of returns

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook supports considering FIRR together with multiples for a realistic performance view, distinguishing gross and net metrics, using public-market benchmarks through KS-PME, considering vintage years, and reviewing track-record metrics such as gross/net IRR, TVPI, DPI, and RVPI in due diligence/PPM disclosures. The Trap: Gross IRR alone ignores fees; lowest fees can hide poor performance; largest corpus does not equal best returns. The source pushes toward combining net metrics, multiples, benchmarks, and disclosures. Note: Earlier wording added "consistent track record across vintage years," vintage-year quartile peer ranking, and a prescriptive preference rule. Those formulations are broader than the checked workbook and have been removed; only the source-listed evaluation inputs remain.
